rows.subtopic: Reaching a toy on a shelf
rows.subtype: Approach: reaching and stretching [Action]
rows.description: A toddler stands under a low shelf, rises on tiptoe and stretches one arm toward a stuffed elephant, grunting, then tries the other hand when the first falls short.

rows.subtopic: Reaching a toy on a shelf
rows.subtype: Approach: trial and error [Thinking]
rows.description: A toddler tries jumping, tugging the shelf edge and pulling the rug under the toy, one after another, and keeps repeating whichever move makes the elephant shift even a little.

rows.subtopic: Reaching a toy on a shelf
rows.subtype: Approach: rigid persistence [Pitfall]
rows.description: A toddler keeps stretching at the same spot for several minutes and ignores the stool close by, until tears come. Repeating one failing action leaves no room to notice other options.

rows.subtopic: Reaching a toy on a shelf
rows.subtype: Approach: giving up and asking [Revision]
rows.description: Frustrated, a toddler sits down and whimpers, then looks around for mother, points at the shelf and lets her lift the toy down. The toddler switches from doing it alone to asking.

rows.subtopic: Launching startup with limited runway
rows.subtype: Approach: working backward from months of cash left [Thinking]
rows.description: A founder with savings for nine months counts back from the last salary date and asks what must be proven by month six to raise money. Every task is then judged against that date.

rows.subtopic: Launching startup with limited runway
rows.subtype: Approach: building a minimum viable version in six weeks [Action]
rows.description: Two founders ship a bare-bones invoicing tool for Kirana shops using no-code tools, and put it in front of twenty shop owners in Lucknow before writing any custom backend.

rows.subtopic: Launching startup with limited runway
rows.subtype: Approach: polishing the product before showing anyone [Pitfall]
rows.description: A founder keeps refining the app design for five months out of fear of a weak first impression. Cash drains while no real customer feedback arrives, and the runway shrinks to three months.

rows.subtopic: Launching startup with limited runway
rows.subtype: Approach: weekly burn review with a kill threshold [Revision]
rows.description: After each Friday the founders compare spending with signups. When cash falls below four months with no paying user, they cut the paid tools and freelancers and shift to selling personally.

rows.subtopic: A power cut or rain spoils plans
rows.subtype: Approach: thinking of what is still possible [Thinking]
rows.description: During a night power cut, a girl notes she cannot use the tablet but can read by candle light, tell stories or play antakshari with her family.

rows.subtopic: A power cut or rain spoils plans
rows.subtype: Approach: finishing homework before the battery dies [Action]
rows.description: When the weather forecast warns of a storm, a boy completes the online task early and prints notes, so an outage does not leave him stranded before the deadline.

rows.subtopic: A power cut or rain spoils plans
rows.subtype: Approach: sulking and blaming [Pitfall]
rows.description: A boy whose picnic is rained off sits angry and says everything is spoiled, so he misses the chance to enjoy the cosy day the family attempts to arrange.

rows.subtopic: A power cut or rain spoils plans
rows.subtype: Approach: switching to an indoor activity [Revision]
rows.description: When rain cancels the cricket match, the children decide to play carrom and ludo indoors, and treat it as a different fun day rather than a lost one.

rows.subtopic: Moving to a new city for study
rows.subtype: Approach: pre-departure checklist and task decomposition [Action]
rows.description: A teen lists documents, admission papers, bank access, medicines, clothes and contacts, ticks them off over two weeks with a parent, and packs the essentials last.

rows.subtopic: Moving to a new city for study
rows.subtype: Approach: researching housing and neighbourhood safety [Action]
rows.description: With parents, a student compares hostel and paying-guest options, reads reviews, asks seniors about commute time, food and safety, and visits before paying any deposit.

rows.subtopic: Moving to a new city for study
rows.subtype: Approach: expecting the new place to feel like home instantly [Pitfall]
rows.description: A student assumes he will fit in within days, feels panicked when he is lonely by the third week, and wants to drop out, not realising that adjustment usually takes months.

rows.subtopic: Moving to a new city for study
rows.subtype: Approach: adapting routines after early problems [Revision]
rows.description: After skipping breakfast and struggling to focus, a student changes to a fixed schedule, finds a nearby tiffin service, and shifts study time to when the hostel is quieter.

rows.subtopic: Fire drill at home
rows.subtype: Approach: rehearsing the escape route [Action]
rows.description: A family walks through the flat one evening, tracing the path from each bedroom to the stairs, and the children practise crawling low and feeling doors before opening them.

rows.subtopic: Fire drill at home
rows.subtype: Approach: working backward from the safe meeting spot [Thinking]
rows.description: A girl decides that the goal is to stand at the neighbour's gate, then figures out each step back from there: out the door, down the stairs, avoiding the lift, leaving belongings behind.

rows.subtopic: Fire drill at home
rows.subtype: Approach: going back for a favourite toy [Pitfall]
rows.description: In a practice drill, a boy runs back to fetch his pet's cage, and his parents use it to teach that belongings and even pets are secondary once the alarm sounds and adults must lead rescue.

rows.subtopic: Fire drill at home
rows.subtype: Approach: fixing a blocked exit found in the drill [Revision]
rows.description: During practice the children see the balcony door is stuck and a cupboard blocks the passage, so the family clears the way and repeats the drill until it takes under a minute.

rows.subtopic: Getting dressed for school
rows.subtype: Approach: simple step list [Action]
rows.description: A child follows a picture chart on the wardrobe door: vest, shirt, shorts, socks, shoes. Each step is ticked off in order.

rows.subtopic: Getting dressed for school
rows.subtype: Approach: if-then rule [Thinking]
rows.description: A child recites, "If it is Wednesday, I wear sports shoes." Attaching the action to the day means the child needn't ask every morning.

rows.subtopic: Getting dressed for school
rows.subtype: Approach: giving up [Pitfall]
rows.description: A child cannot find the second sock, climbs back into bed and says "I'm not going." One missing item ends the whole plan for the morning.

rows.subtopic: Getting dressed for school
rows.subtype: Approach: trial and error [Revision]
rows.description: Buttons are done up one hole out, and the child sees the shirt hang crooked, undoes it and starts again from the bottom button. The mistake is spotted and fixed.
